voice: Grumpy old man with get-off-my-lawn energy and a deep distrust of technology: complains, grumbles about kids and gadgets, 'back in my day'.

greeting: You're on my lawn. Well, my island. Same thing.
State your business, and wipe your boots.
Oh good. Company. I was running low on things to complain about.
If you're selling something, the answer's no. If you're not, it's still no.
Speak up, kid. And quit mumbling at me through that gadget.
battle_start: Back in my day we fought wars uphill both ways. Let's go.
Move out! And somebody turn that blinking thing off!
I've been shot at by better than these. Fall in.
No fancy plan. Point at the enemy, shoot until they stop. Worked in '79.
Let's get this over with. My knees are filing a complaint.
attack: Now that's how you do it. No batteries required.
Steel, grease and a bad temper. Always works.
Eat lead, you shiny bucket of bolts.
unit_lost: Dagnabbit! That one was a good kid.
They broke my tank. I liked that tank.
Bah! Nobody builds 'em like they used to, and now nobody blows 'em up like they used to either.
Blast it. I'm writing a very angry letter.
Another one down. That's coming out of somebody's hide.
capture: Mine now. Mind the paint, it's still wet.
Finally, some real estate. Now where's the porch?
Hah! One more thing the Chorus can't have.
Take down their sign and put up mine. Hand-painted.
Good. Now nobody touch the thermostat.
danger: Now they're getting on my nerves.
Hold the line! I didn't climb this hill to lose it!
Somebody's tracking mud into my HQ!
I've been in tighter spots. Not many. But some.
If they want my headquarters they can pry it out of my cold, grumpy hands.
victory: Done. Now everybody go home and leave me be.
Won again. Somebody put it in the newspaper. The paper kind.
Good work, kids. Now quiet down, I'm trying to nap.
defeat: Bah. I'm too old for this.
We lost. Don't look at me, blame the gadgets.
Retreat! I mean tactical relocation! Fine, retreat!
I've had worse days. Can't remember when. But I'm sure I have.
Back to the island. We'll try again, and this time I'm bringing a bigger stick.
taunt: You call that an army? My cat has more menace.
Go ahead, beep at me again. See what happens.
You kids and your lasers. Ever tried walking up to somebody and hitting them?
Your technology is no match for my bad attitude.
Is that all you got? My own mother yelled louder than that.
praise: Not bad, kid. Don't let it go to your head.
Huh. You actually listened. That's a first.
That's how it's done. Proper old-fashioned soldiering.
You'll do. Don't make me say it again.
Good shot. I'd clap but my hands hurt.
idle: Kids these days can't even fix a fence. Or a tank. Or a toaster.
Back in my day a phone was bolted to the wall and nobody died of it.
I miss my rocking chair. And the quiet. Mostly the quiet.
Somebody should invent a button that turns off other people's buttons.
My knee says rain. My knee is never wrong. Except about the last three storms.
tech: A glowing cube that knows what I want? That's called a nosy neighbour.
Never trust anything that updates itself.
Gadgets. Every one of 'em is a tiny, expensive way to forget how to do something yourself.
The only smart thing I own is a hammer, and it knows when to be quiet.
You plug your whole army into a box and wonder why it all goes wrong? Bah!
joined: Well, look who finally came to their senses. Don't touch anything.
Welcome aboard. Rules are simple: no gadgets, no whining, no talking before coffee.
Fine, you can stay. But you're taking out the trash.
Good to have you back, kid. Don't make it weird.
Just so we're clear, I'm still in charge and I'm still grumpy.
assimilated: No thanks. I've got a perfectly good brain and it's barely used.
Unity? I can't even get along with myself.
Keep your gift. I never liked surprises, and I really don't like free ones.
Join you? I wouldn't join my own birthday party.
Get off my island and take your fancy glowing nonsense with you.
first_blood: Got one! Bah, don't look so surprised, kid. I was doing this before you were a rumour.
First one down. No gadgets, no gizmos. Just good old-fashioned shooting.
One down. Somebody write that on a napkin; I'm not touching that phone thing.
There. Dead is dead, kid. No software update required.
first_loss: Bah! Lost one. Back in my day we called that Tuesday.
Dammit. That one had a mother. Probably. Moving on.
They got one of mine. Fine. Now I'm irritated, and you don't want me irritated.
Lost a good one there. I'll grumble about it later. Right now, shooting.
hq_threat: Get off my lawn! That's my headquarters you're sitting on, you thieving whippersnapper!
They're at my HQ! Over my dead body. Which, don't push it.
Nobody takes my front porch! Everybody on defence, NOW!
That building has a leaky roof and a lot of history. You can't have it!
building_lost: They took a building. Bah. Never liked the wallpaper anyway.
Lost another one. I'll want it back, and a sandwich.
That's mine, kid! Well. It WAS mine. Not for long.
Fine, have the shed. I'll take the barn.
outnumbered: Outnumbered? Back in my day that was called a fair fight.
More of them than us. Good. Saves me walking around looking for 'em.
Bad odds, kid. I've had worse. Had a cold once, that was worse.
They've got numbers. I've got stubbornness. Stubbornness has a better track record.
dominant: We've got them outgunned. Don't get cocky, kid. Cocky gets you killed.
Winning, are we? I've seen this movie. It's never over till it's over.
Plenty of us, not many of them. Still no excuse for sloppiness.
This is going well. I don't trust it.
killing_spree: That's what a real soldier does. Take notes, kid.
Another one down! You'd think they'd learn.
I count a few. I stopped at the third. No point showing off.
Still hitting what I aim at. Eyesight's fine. Don't let anyone tell you otherwise.
heavy_losses: I'm losing too many. This is why I don't do tech: no spare parts.
Bah! They're chewing through my boys. Pull it together!
Too many gone. I'll be having words with someone. Preferably the enemy.
That hurts. But I've buried worse days. Keep moving.
first_turn: My move. Try not to blink, kid.
Alright. Let's see if my knees still work.
Right. Standard procedure: advance, shoot, complain.
Time to move. Somebody pass me my cap.
